primary_meaning: God's people (Israel in the OT; the Church/believers in the NT) as the flock under the care, guidance, and protection of the divine Shepherd (God or Christ)

alternatives.meaning: The righteous/elect (as distinguished from goats representing the unrighteous) at the final judgment
Vulnerable, dependent, or wayward humans prone to go astray and needing rescue
Meek, innocent, or sacrificial figures (often overlapping with 'lamb' imagery)

notes: Christian tradition from the early church onward consistently treats sheep as the people of God under pastoral care; the shepherd-sheep metaphor is one of the most stable and frequently invoked biblical images across OT and NT.
